特别处档案室。
档案号：7.0.1466。

事由

马克斯·克里沃勒（Max Krivoller）关于为俄国政府进行药品交易的陈述。

涉及人员：
S. 戈尔茨坦（S. Goldstein），美国人。
贝特尔（Berthel）。
弗洛伊德（Eloyd），《字林西报》（Shanghai Times）职员。

1466
24/9/17

September 24, 7.

Sir Everard D. H. Fraser, K.C.M.G.,
H. B. M's Consul-General,
Shanghai.

My dear Sir Everard, Confidential.

Max Kindler on September 22 made and
signed a statement to the following effect:-

"A little over a year ago, a certain chemist staying
in the boarding house of Mrs Abeles at 23 North Szechuen
Road, got in contact with certain Russians, who wished
to buy medicine for the Russian Government. A deal was
arranged through an American named S. Goldstein. The
chemist and Goldstein went to Berthel, and asked if he
could supply the medicine wanted. He replied in the
affirmative, adding that he would need a few days' grace.

"Berthel supplied the wanted drugs which bore labels
of British manufacturers. The cargo was shipped and the
Russo-Asiatic Bank paid for them against the Bill of
lading. When the medicine arrived in Russia it was found
that some of it which purported to be quinine and other
drugs was composed of flour, epsom salts, and other worth-
less ingredients. The Russian Government moved in the
matter, and, as a result, some lawyer in Shanghai wrote
very strongly to Goldstein and Berthel saying they would
be prosecuted if they did not return the money. Berthel
then engaged Dr. Fischer, and did not return the money."

Yours sincerely,

Captain-Superintendent of Police.

1917年9月24日

致
埃弗拉德·D·H·弗雷泽爵士（Sir Everard D. H. Fraser），K.C.M.G.，
英国驻上海总领事。

亲爱的弗雷泽爵士，机密。

马克斯·金德勒（Max Kindler）于9月22日作出并签署了一份声明，内容如下：

“一年多以前，一位寄住在北四川路23号阿贝莱斯夫人（Mrs Abeles）寄宿公寓的药剂师，与一些希望为俄国政府购买药品的俄国人取得了联系。这笔交易是通过一位名叫 S. 戈尔茨坦（S. Goldstein）的美国人安排的。该药剂师和戈尔茨坦去找贝特尔（Berthel），询问他能否供应所需的药品。他给予了肯定的答复，并补充说需要几天的宽限期。

贝特尔提供了所需的药物，这些药物贴有英国制造商的标签。货物装船发运，华俄道胜银行（Russo-Asiatic Bank）凭提单支付了货款。当药品抵达俄国时，发现其中一些声称是奎宁和其他药物的物品实际上是由面粉、泻盐（epsom salts）和其他无价值的成分组成的。俄国政府对此事采取了行动，结果，上海的一位律师措辞严厉地致函戈尔茨坦和贝特尔，称如果他们不退还钱款，将对他们提起诉讼。随后，贝特尔聘请了费舍尔博士（Dr. Fischer），并未退还款项。”

此致，

警务处处长。

POLICE FORCE.
(DETECTIVE BRANCH.)

24th September 1917.

Sir,
Max Kindler on September 22nd made andsigned a
statement to the following effect:-
"A little over a year ago, a certain chemist staying
in the boarding house of Mrs. Abeles at 23 North
Szechuen Road, got in contact with certain Russians,
who wished to buy medicine for the Russian Government.
A deal was arranged through an American named S. Goldstein.
The chemist and Goldstein went to Berthel, and asked
if he could supply the medicine wanted.. He replied in
the affirmative, adding that he would need a few days'
grace.
"Berthel supplied the wanted drugs which bore labels
of British manufacturers. The cargo was shipped and
the Russo-Asiatic Bank paid for them against the Bill
of lading. When the medicine arrived in Russia it was
found that some of it which purported to be quinine
and other drugs was composed of flour, epsom salts, and
other worthless ingredients. The Russian Government
moved in the matter, and, as a result, some lawyer in
Shanghai wrote very strongly to Goldstein and Berthel
saying they would be prosecuted if they did not return
the money. Berthel then engaged Dr. Fischer, and did
not return the money."

Your obedient servant,

i/c C.I.D.

Captain Superintendent of Police.
